posts.content:
adding 5 internal links to a page sounds too simple to move rankings

until you see a page jump from page 2 to page 1 without a single new backlink

that’s when internal linking starts looking a lot less “basic”

the reason is simple

google doesn’t just look at what’s on the page

it also looks at how the rest of your site treats that page

if a service page is buried 4 clicks deep with 2 weak internal links pointing to it, you’re basically telling google:

“this page isn’t that important”

then people wonder why it sits at #11 for 6 months

what i do instead:

> find pages already ranking between #5-15

> find the strongest relevant pages on the site

> add contextual internal links from those pages

> use natural anchors that actually describe the target page

> don’t repeat the exact same anchor 20 times

> prioritize links from pages that already have traffic, backlinks or strong rankings

the key is relevance

a random link from an unrelated blog post won’t do much

but if you have a strong page about “AC repair” linking naturally into your “AC replacement” page, that signal actually makes sense

and this is why internal links can move pages faster than people expect

the page is already close

google already understands it

you’re just making it clearer which pages on your site matter most

before buying another backlink, i’d check this first

you might already have the authority

you’re just sending it to the wrong places
posts.author: Sarvesh Shrivastava
posts.notes: 内部链接策略可与外链建设互补，提升页面权重。

comments.author: Giovanni Labs
comments.text: Same holds on YouTube. End screens and description links between your own videos let one view lead to the next. It's the cheapest lever most channels ignore.

comments.author: Kam Hossieny | CRO
comments.text: internal links are underrated, especially when they help distribute authority to pages already close to ranking.
